title: Submodular Benchmark Selection
abstract: arXiv:2605.02209v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Evaluating a new language model means running it on a large, growing collection of benchmarks, at considerable cost. Much of this cost is redundant: arranged as a matrix of models by benchmarks, scores are strongly correlated and concentrate in a few dimensions, so a few well-chosen benchmarks largely determine the rest. This allows us to run a new model on a few benchmarks and predict the rest with a simple Gaussian model that copes with missing scores. The key question is \emph{which few to run}. An answer comes from sensor placement, which chooses the observations that carry the most information, measured by entropy or mutual information. We argue that the objective should instead reward a selection for how well it predicts every benchmark. This leads to two coverage objectives: explained variance, the predictions' accuracy if the estimated correlations were exact, and facility location, which credits each benchmark with its best

translated_abstract: 评估一个新的语言模型意味着要在一个庞大且不断增长的基准测试集合上运行它，这需要相当高的成本。而这些成本中的很大一部分是冗余的：如果把分数排列成一个“模型×基准”的矩阵，分数之间呈现强相关性，并集中在少数几个维度上，因此少数精心挑选的基准在很大程度上就能决定其余基准的分数。这使得我们可以让新模型只在少数基准上运行，并用一个能够处理缺失分数的简单高斯模型来预测其余基准的分数。关键问题在于“应该运行哪少数几个基准”。一个答案来自传感器布置问题，它选择携带信息量最大的观测点，并以熵或互信息来度量信息量。我们认为，目标函数应当改为奖励那些能够很好地预测所有基准的选择。这引出了两个覆盖目标：解释方差——即在估计的相关性完全准确的情况下预测所能达到的准确度；以及设施选址——它为每个基准记入其最好的……
tldr: 该论文提出用次模优化中的覆盖目标（解释方差和设施选址）来挑选少数信息量最大的评测基准，使得只需在新模型上运行少量基准，即可用高斯模型准确预测其余所有基准的分数，从而大幅降低语言模型评测成本。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes selecting a small subset of benchmarks using submodular coverage objectives (explained variance and facility location), so that a new language model only needs to be evaluated on a few benchmarks whose scores can accurately predict all remaining benchmarks via a Gaussian model, greatly reducing evaluation costs.
